Rider Comms Terms of Use

Last updated: 1 October 2026

These terms are an agreement between you and [Company legal name] for your use of Rider Comms (the app and web app). By creating an account you agree to them, to our Community Guidelines and to our Privacy Policy. There is no tolerance for objectionable content or abusive behaviour.

1. Riding safety comes first

  • Rider Comms is a companion for riding. It is not a substitute for your own attention, judgment, training, or the rules of the road.
  • Don't look at or touch the app while moving. Stop somewhere safe before using visual or touch controls. The app locks distracting controls when it detects sustained movement. That lock is an aid, not a guarantee.
  • Use only hands-free, legally permitted equipment (such as a helmet intercom) and follow local laws on device use while riding.
  • Navigation, hazard reports and nearby-rider information can be wrong, late or missing. Routes may be unsuitable or unsafe. Reports come from other riders and aren't verified. Always follow road signs, conditions and the law.
  • Don't use Rider Comms to coordinate illegal riding, racing, or evading enforcement. [Legal review: police/camera report features and local law.]

2. Your account

  • You must be at least 16 and able to form a binding contract.
  • Keep your password secret. You're responsible for activity on your account.
  • Give accurate information, and don't impersonate anyone.
  • You can delete your account at any time in Settings.

3. Community rules

You must not use Rider Comms to:

  • harass, threaten, bully, stalk or intimidate anyone, including by misusing location or ride features;
  • share sexual content, content that sexualises minors, or hateful, violent or dangerous content;
  • send spam, scams or unsolicited promotion;
  • file false hazard or safety reports;
  • share someone else's location or personal information without their permission;
  • break the law, or infringe other people's rights;
  • interfere with the service: scraping, reverse engineering, overloading it, getting around rate limits or blocks, or accessing accounts that aren't yours.

4. Reporting, moderation and suspension

You can report and block other riders. We review reports within 24 hours and may remove content, restrict features, or suspend or terminate accounts that break these terms or put others at risk, with or without notice where safety requires. You can appeal a decision by contacting [support email]; someone other than the original moderator will review it.

5. Content you share

You keep ownership of what you post (such as messages, profile details and hazard reports). You give us a licence to host, store and show it to the riders you choose, only to run Rider Comms. Hazard reports are shown to nearby riders and expire automatically.

6. Third-party services

Maps, place search and navigation use Google Maps Platform, and voice uses LiveKit. Your use of those features is also subject to the Google Maps/Google Earth Additional Terms of Service and our providers' policies. Handing off to Google Maps, Waze or Apple Maps opens those apps under their own terms.

7. Paid plans

Rider Comms is free to use. Premium and Premium+ widen your Nearby range (to 6 and 20 miles; Free is 1 mile) and are sold only in the iPhone and Android apps, as auto-renewing monthly subscriptions through the Apple App Store or Google Play. The price is shown before you buy.

  • Payment is charged to your Apple Account or Google Play account when you confirm the purchase.
  • A subscription renews automatically each month at the same price unless you cancel it at least 24 hours before the end of the current period. Your account is charged for the renewal within the 24 hours before the period ends.
  • You can manage or cancel a subscription in your App Store or Google Play account settings. Cancelling stops the next renewal; you keep your plan until the end of the period you've paid for.
  • Refunds are handled by Apple or Google under their policies.
  • A subscription is linked to the Rider Comms account that first used it. Use "Restore purchases" on the plan screen to link it again after reinstalling. Deleting your Rider Comms account doesn't cancel a subscription; cancel it in your store settings.
  • If we change a subscription's price, the store tells you first, as its rules require.

8. Availability and changes

Rider Comms is provided "as is" and may change, be interrupted, or be discontinued. Features that depend on your connection, GPS or device permissions may not always work. We may update these terms, and will give notice in the app of material changes.

10. Ending your use

You can stop using Rider Comms and delete your account at any time. We may suspend or end your access under section 4. Sections that by their nature should survive (for example 5, 9 and 11) continue after termination.
